newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat harvest moves ahead amid hot weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat harvest moves ahead amid hot weather.

text.p: Harvesting of the Texas wheat crop was active as hot, open weather prevailed during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Wheat was 76 percent harvested, lagging 89 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 85 percent, but up from 52 percent a week ago.
"Yields continued to be better than earlier expected in many dryland fields," the report said.
Wheat crop condition was rated 41 percent good to excellent, against 51 percent at the same level a week ago.

Corn condition declined slightly and was rated 84 percent good to excellent, against 88 at that level a week ago. Corn was 55 percent silked versus 64 a year ago and the average of 65 percent. Sorghum was four percent mature, ahead of 22 percent both last year and on average.

Growth of the state's cotton improved dramatically in the Plains under the hot conditions and along with recent rains. Cotton was 55 percent in good to excellent condition, ahead of 50 percent at that level last week. Thirteen percent of the crop had set bolls, versus 17 last year and 18 on average.
